post_text:
Distributed systems lack a global clock.

Relying on wall-clock timestamps for event ordering is a fast track to data corruption. 🕒

Use partition keys to force related events into the same consumer thread.

This ensures sequential processing at the infrastructure level before your code even touches the payload.

Implement idempotent consumers with version-based fencing to ignore stale updates.

A late "Update" event must never overwrite a newer "Delete" state in your database.

Your business logic must reject any event with a version lower than the current state recorded in the persistence layer.

Replace system timestamps with sequence numbers or vector clocks to define absolute order.

Logical clocks are the only way to guarantee causality across distributed nodes.

Clock drift is inevitable; your architecture must be immune to it. 🛠️
lesson_extracted: Rely on logical sequence numbers and partitioning rather than system timestamps to guarantee event ordering in distributed architectures.
